name: Bayesian / particle-filter geosteering: Veettil & Clark SMC geosteering (2020); Muhammad, Srivastava, Alyaev et al. RL + particle filter (2024/2025); ROGII Kaggle PF components
authors_org: D. R. A. Veettil & K. Clark (Petrophysics 2020); R. B. Muhammad, A. Srivastava, S. Alyaev, R. B. Bratvold, D. M. Tartakovsky (UiS / NORCE / Stanford); ROGII Kaggle 1st/3rd/4th/5th place PF components
year: 2020 (SMC geosteering); 2024 arXiv / 2025 Computational Geosciences (RL+PF); 2026 (Kaggle ROGII PF variants)
venue_link: Petrophysics 61(1):99-111, doi:10.30632/PJV61N1-2020a4 (https://onepetro.org/petrophysics/article-abstract/61/01/99/171623); Computational Geosciences 29, art. 14 (2025), arXiv:2402.06377 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06377); ROGII 3rd-place writeup (https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rogii-wellbore-geology-prediction/writeups/3rd-place-solution)
code_availability: No public code for Veettil & Clark or the RL+PF paper. NORCE code hub: https://github.com/geosteering-no (benchmark, DISTINGUISH, 10000 GWC interpretations). A PF already exists in our repo: rogii_champion/src/particle_filter.py (512 particles; state = level, structural slope, GR bias; 3 profiles; genealogy backward pass), glue in kaggle2ndplace/anchor_pf.py and anchor_pfchan.py; the 1st-place pipeline has PF-heatmap config (experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_cfg.py PF_heatmap_*: 500 particles x 128 seeds).
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (Petrophysics 2020; Computational Geosciences 2025), plus Kaggle competition writeups (1st/3rd/4th place PF numbers), plus our own holdout logs
extreme_summary: Treat the well's stratigraphic position (plus dip and GR bias) as a hidden Markov state and track it along MD with a sequential Monte Carlo filter whose likelihood compares lateral GR to the typewell; the particle cloud is a non-Gaussian, possibly multimodal posterior. In ROGII it is a weak standalone predictor (6.6-7.4 ft for winners, 13.1 ft for ours) but a decorrelated feature/channel source.
task_definition: Sequentially estimate the tool position relative to stratigraphic layers (equivalently TVT along the lateral) and stratigraphic variables (boundary depths / dip) from LWD measurements as the well is drilled; in RL+PF the estimate feeds a DQN steering policy.
inputs: Lateral gamma ray, a typewell / offset-well GR reference (GWC 2020 logs in Muhammad et al.), well trajectory (inclination / TVD), prior on layer structure; in Kaggle variants also the known heel TVT prefix and optionally sibling-well lateral GR as an alternative reference.
target_parameterisation: Explicit state space: Veettil & Clark estimate stratigraphic variables jointly with tool location; Muhammad et al. state = reservoir boundary positions b_x on a 10 ft MD grid; our PF and ROGII 3rd: structural coordinate S = TVT + Z with a slope/rate state (dTVT = r*dMD - dZ) plus GR bias and observation-family flags.
output_representation: Weighted particle cloud (empirical posterior). Summaries used: best particle (MAP-like) and top-5 weighted particles (Muhammad et al.); weighted mean, q10-q90, spread, skew, IQR (ROGII 3rd); 2D particle-probability heatmap on the TVT x MD grid (ROGII 1st); Gaussian bump + confidence (our pf_bump/pf_conf channels).
architecture: Bootstrap particle filter: propagate particles with a random-walk (with momentum) transition on position/slope/bias, including rare large jumps for faults; weight by a GR likelihood (Gaussian sigma=0.2 on normalised GR in Muhammad et al.; Student-t df=2 in our PF); systematic resampling when ESS falls below a threshold (or at fixed points before each decision in Muhammad et al.); optional backward smoothing through particle genealogy; several configuration profiles / seeds blended. Muhammad et al. used 128 particles (tested 32-1024); ROGII 3rd used 500 particles x 240 seeds; our PF 512 particles x 3 profiles, updates in 64 ft MD bins.
core_mechanism: Bayesian recursive filtering handles the nonlinear, non-Gaussian observation model (GR vs depth is many-to-one when layers repeat), so several stratigraphic hypotheses can coexist in the particle cloud until later GR disambiguates them. The explicit slope state encodes the physical prior that dip changes slowly, which constrains drift.
training_objective: None for the filter itself (pure inference; hyperparameters hand-tuned or grid-searched). Muhammad et al. train only the downstream DQN policy. ROGII 4th trained a LightGBM residual corrector (L2+L1 blend) on ~115 PF self-diagnostic features.
decoding: Best particle or top-5 particles (Muhammad et al.); weighted mean of genealogy-smoothed paths, with seed paths weighted by full-sequence likelihood (ROGII 3rd; our PF); forward + backward runs (ROGII 4th).
metric_consistent_decode: Mixed: the weighted mean of smoothed particles is RMSE-consistent; best-particle / top-k decodes (Muhammad et al.) are mode-seeking and would raise our pooled RMSE under band ambiguity.
evidence_scope: Whole lateral processed sequentially (causal forward filter, optional backward smoothing) against the typewell; ROGII 3rd also uses sibling-well references.
prefix_conditioning: In ROGII variants the known heel prefix initialises particles tightly at the last known row and calibrates the typewell GR mapping; in the geosteering papers the prior comes from the pre-drill geomodel.
propose_vs_select: Proposes a distribution / many candidate paths; ROGII 1st and 3rd use it as a candidate and feature generator feeding a NN or gate rather than as the final output.
physical_constraints: Smooth dip (random walk on slope with momentum), rare fault jumps, TVT+Z structural identity (our PF, ROGII 3rd), slowly drifting GR bias, heavy-tailed GR likelihood.
dataset: Veettil & Clark: simulated formation-tops examples. Muhammad et al.: synthetic geomodels built from real GR logs of the Geosteering World Cup 2020 semifinal. ROGII Kaggle: real laterals with typewells; our holdout = 155 wells.
synthetic_to_real: The filter needs no training data, so there is no learned synthetic-to-real gap; the gap appears as typewell-vs-lateral GR mismatch, handled by the GR bias state, typewell calibration ('seen_blend' in the 1st-place cfg) and heavy-tailed likelihoods.
metric_and_performance: Muhammad et al.: best-particle GR MAE 0.0099 (normalised) with 128 particles, yet boundary estimates can disagree with truth (multimodality); RL with PF estimates reached 88.67% reservoir contact vs 66.84% using raw logs, within 1-2% of an oracle given true boundaries. ROGII 3rd: PF CV 6.58 / public 7.01 / private 6.73 ft RMSE. ROGII 1st: PF standalone CV ~7.4 ft; PF channels cut CV 7.7 -> 6.7 early, but gave no gain for the final strong single model. Ours (155 holdout wells): PF standalone best 13.07 ft (runs/X_pf_final), residual correlation 0.31 with rb_v3_tta_ep150 (4.94 ft), best blend weight 0.03 for -0.014 ft; AnchorCNN with PF channels (runs/C_pf_far_ep250) 7.35 ft pooled.
comparability: Kaggle PF numbers are CV/LB RMSE in ft on the same competition data but other splits; our 13.07 ft and 7.35 ft are on our 155-well holdout. Journal results are not comparable (synthetic, boundary/decision metrics).
validation_protocol: Journal work: synthetic scenarios only. ROGII 3rd reported CV vs public vs private (small PF gap 6.58/7.01/6.73), consistent with a training-free method having no selection bias. Our PF is training-free, so fold safety is trivial (anchor_pfchan.py documents no tvt leakage).
inference_budget: Cheap CPU: our PF ~24 ms per well per profile in numpy; 3rd place's 500 x 240-seed version is much heavier but still CPU-feasible offline; fits the Kaggle budget.
repeated_layers: In principle multiple hypotheses stay alive in the particle cloud; in practice ESS-triggered resampling collapses minority modes and the PF commits to a wrong band (Muhammad et al. note the multimodality; ROGII 4th calls wrong-layer matches the main PF failure and mitigates with bidirectional decoding, a Viterbi second opinion with typewell-rung 'aliasing companions' and a learned corrector). ROGII 3rd kept hard/soft observation families and typewell vs sibling reference flags to preserve diversity.
drift: An explicit slope/rate state with momentum (3rd place rate momentum 0.9995) models a straight-line structural trend, which matches the one-line-per-well drift mode; PF drift mostly comes from a mis-set initial rate or GR bias.
uncertainty_and_calibration: Particle spread is an uncertainty proxy; our logs show Spearman rho 0.37-0.58 between PF spread and |error| (rank-informative, not calibrated). No reliability/ECE analysis in the papers. Likelihood temperature (obs_temp, lik_scale) is the main calibration knob.
where_to_use: (1) Input channels to the ConvNeXt/FastViT U-Net (the 1st-place code path exists: PF_heatmap_* in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_cfg.py). (2) Rich per-row features (quantiles, spread, skew, forward/backward disagreement) for a gate or residual corrector. (3) A test-time tracker that uses the U-Net posterior as its emission model (see B06).
error_mode_targeted: Drift (~25%) via the explicit slope state; secondarily band confusion (~51%) by adding sequential whole-lateral evidence.
gap_vs_our_implementation: [uncertain] We already have a PF (rogii_champion/src/particle_filter.py) and tried it as a blend member (weight 0.02-0.03, at most 0.014 ft gain) and as channels on AnchorCNN (7.35 ft, far from 4.84 ft). Gaps: (a) our PF is about 2x worse than winners' (13.07 vs 6.6-7.4 ft); missing vs 3rd place: many more seeds (240 vs 3 profiles), hard/soft observation-family mixtures, sibling-reference particles, rate momentum, likelihood-weighted seed averaging. (b) We export only a Gaussian bump + confidence (pf_bump/pf_conf); winners exported the full 2D particle heatmap (1st) or q10-q90/spread/skew/IQR plus row differences (3rd). A single-Gaussian summary discards exactly the multimodal information relevant to band confusion. (c) Our best ConvNeXt/FastViT runs appear to use the default channel set without PF heatmap channels; 1st place kept PF-channel models (0729_V3, 0803_V2) only for ensemble diversity. (d) No PF variant uses the network's own posterior as emission, and none uses mode-preserving resampling (clustered / regularised) to keep minority bands alive. (e) Joint estimation of typewell stretch / thickness (Veettil & Clark's stratigraphic variables) is absent from our state (L, r, b).
proposed_experiment: E1 (cheap, most direct): train FastViT-SA12 (distilled) with the 1st-place 2D PF heatmap channels enabled in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_cfg.py (PF_heatmap_n_particles=500, PF_heatmap_n_seeds=128; PF rotate/shift corruption augmentation on), 150 epochs, same seed; control = current 4.84 ft student. Score with seq_NN_holdout_eval.py and seq_NN_robust_compare.py on the 155 holdout wells; accept if gain exceeds the 0.39 ft noise floor, or if RMSE is equal but residual correlation with the non-PF model drops enough to improve the best pair (4.69 ft). E2: upgrade rogii_champion/src/particle_filter.py toward the 3rd-place spec (more seeds, hard/soft families, rate momentum) and export q10/q25/q50/q75/q90 + spread channels instead of pf_bump/pf_conf in kaggle2ndplace/anchor_pfchan.py; gate on standalone PF holdout RMSE < 9 ft before any NN retraining. E3 (diagnostic, no training): on posteriors from seq_NN_posterior_dump.py --save-all, check per well whether the PF modal band is correct on the U-Net's wrong_mode wells; if yes on a meaningful share, the PF carries evidence the network lacks and E1/E2 are worth running.
implementation_effort: Low for E1 (code path exists in the 1st-place config; mainly PF cache generation for real and synthetic wells); medium for E2 (PF engineering and tuning); low for E3 (analysis only).
gpu_cost: [uncertain] PF is CPU-only (tens of ms per well per profile; 128 seeds x 500 particles cached once, likely minutes to about an hour for all wells). E1 retraining costs about one normal 150-epoch run on the RTX 5060 8 GB; 2-3 extra input channels add negligible memory.
distillation_compatibility: Yes: PF features are inputs, so teacher and student both consume them and KD on output posteriors is unchanged. PF features must also be computed for synthetic training wells (1st place cached them).
error_correlation_with_ours: High diversity as a standalone member (residual correlation 0.20-0.33 with the ConvNeXt) but too inaccurate to earn blend weight; as a channel the diversity is partly absorbed. 1st place kept PF-channel models specifically as decorrelated ensemble members.
risk: 1st place found PF channels stopped helping once backbones and augmentation became stronger; our AnchorCNN PF-channel result (7.35 ft) never became competitive. Shortcut learning: the network may copy the PF path (1st place needed PF rotate/shift corruption). Resampling collapses minority modes, so PF evidence for the correct band may be missing exactly where needed. Our PF is much weaker than winners', and improving it costs engineering time for a payoff that may sit inside the +-0.39 ft noise floor.
notes: [uncertain] Muhammad et al. acknowledge multimodality and found top-5 particles gave insignificant gains over the best particle for decision quality (a decision metric, not RMSE). The 7.35 ft 'Ruby PF' in our notes appears to correspond to kaggle2ndplace/runs/C_pf_far_ep250 (AnchorCNN + PF channels, effnet, 250 epochs). The Geosciences 2024 paper 'Real-Time Automated Geosteering Interpretation Combining Log Interpretation and 3D Horizon Tracking' (doi:10.3390/geosciences14030071) adds seismic horizon tracking, which ROGII lacks. Related items: A09 (multi-realization interpretation), B06 (differentiable PF).
